items.title: How Raised Revenue Guidance At Garmin (GRMN) Has Changed Its Investment Story
items.summary: Garmin reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$1,986.08 million and net income of US$541.66 million, then raised full year revenue guidance to about US$8.15b while signalling continued pressure in domain controllers and Auto OEM. The combination of higher earnings per share, increased repurchase activity and fresh high end cycling product launches highlights Garmin’s focus on profitable growth and a deeper fitness ecosystem, despite segment specific headwinds. items.title: Garmin (GRMN) Stock Looks Like It Trades At A Discount
items.summary: Garmin has delivered a strong multi‑year share price run and fresh record results, so the key issue now is whether the current US$272.67 tag still lines up with the cash the business is expected to produce. With a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view available, the question is how that intrinsic value estimate stacks up against a stock that has already rewarded long term holders. items.summary: Garmin (GRMN) just paired a strong Q3 2026 earnings release with higher full year guidance, even as it flags softer automotive domain controller demand and rising memory costs as near term pressure points. items.title: Garmin (GRMN) Stock Sinks After Q3 Results Defy Margin Doubts
items.summary: Garmin just reported Q3 2026 and the headline looks clean. Revenue landed at about US$2.0b with pro forma earnings per share of US$2.76 and gross margin near 63%. Yet the stock dropped almost 6% on the day. That is sentiment running hotter than the numbers. The key story is margin strength.
